title: Norwegian smoke-hot Norwegian Charred lamb Stew
description: A rich and indulgent Norwegian dish featuring charred lamb in a smoky sauce, perfect for a raw-friendly hot pot meal. This stew combines the flavors of capers and lamb for a truly unforgettable experience.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the lamb cubes and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the smoked paprika, lamb broth, red wine, tomato paste, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Transfer the Dutch oven to the preheated oven and braise the lamb for 2 1/2 hours, or until tender and falling apart.
Meanwhile, cook the egg noodles according to package instructions and set aside.
When the lamb is done, stir in the chopped parsley and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve the lamb and juices over the cooked egg noodles, with lemon wedges on the side.
Garnish with additional parsley and capers, if desired.
This stew is perfect for a raw-friendly hot pot meal, as the lamb is slow-cooked to tender perfection and the flavors are rich and indulgent.
The capers add a salty and tangy flavor, while the smoked paprika gives the dish a smoky and savory taste.
This dish is sure to become a favorite among lamb lovers and hot pot enthusiasts alike.
The prep time is approximately 20 minutes, and the cooking time is about 2 1/2 hours.
The total time is approximately 2 3/4 hours, and the servings are 4-6.
This stew is rated as medium difficulty due to the time required for braising the lamb, but the end result is well worth the effort.
